chapter: Church, Bel Canto and the return to music
title: Babs Gonzales and the stolen book of slang
summary: Babs Gonzales had his slang book published by a disc jockey and became bitter; she tried to calm him.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: But getting back to Babs Gonzales, you know I haven't told you something about this terrific character that's so fantastic. He wrote some of the greatest books on the slang idiom. He became so abused and confused about people taking his compositions and things that he had written He used to live down the street from me and on his way to the subway he would pass here every day. He said, "Listen Mary, I've written a book." He took this book to a disc jockey... This guy used his entire book and had it published under his name, Fred Robinson. So Babs said, "Oh, that's all right," and he used to dance around. The next thing musicians were recording his compositions and what-not and he became so bitter about it till he began to go

around town fighting. I used to meet him and he'd say, "Lou, I'm really sick of what they're doing to me." He was so talented; he could create all these various things that he sang. I was trying to baby him. I said, "Oh, Babs, don't do that." One time he went down to the Roost - or Broadway I think it was the Roost, Rooster or something like that - and Erroll Garner was playing and he started some stuff there. They said Babs used to carry red pepper in his hands. He was under a fan and he was trying to throw this in the manager's eyes and the fan blew it back in his eyes. He was going all around town just in a bad way. So I said, "Babs, if I were you I wouldn't do that." He said "What let people take advantage of you and steal all your material and that everything?" And from that day on was the nicest guy that I've ever seen in my life. He used to get jobs for anybody that was out of work and do the craziest and nicest things for them and all of a sudden he changed, losing so much. One day I got kind of angry because somebody owed me some royalties and he met me downtown. I was puffing and blowing... and I was so mad. He said, "Oh, so you're the lady that told me to stop fighting!" But I've seen some of the material he's written and it's so different and so great. I've just heard here recently, and I've just said to myself, I'll be glad when he gets back the way he used to be.
